subject: Order Form: pen test gating, SOC 2 scope & evidence workback
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@heliotherapy.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Chen <mchen@heliotherapy.com>; security_ops@heliotherapy.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Order form security exhibit — pen test gating and SOC2 evidence cadence

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. As we prepare the final order form and exhibit our security team asked for a short writeup on three items so we can clear procurement:

1) Pen test gating — what exactly needs to be in place before a customer-run or vendor-contracted penetration test is permitted (staging access, whitelisting, notification window, escrow contact).
2) SOC 2 evidence cadence — your proposed cadence for delivering artifacts, sample sets, and the SOC 2 report (our compliance requires a minimum of quarterly evidence availability for a rolling 12 months).
3) Staging access and data handling — ephemeral credentials, IP restrictions, and whether logs/audit trails will be retained for X days post-test.

We've attached our high-level vendor_pen_test_scope.xlsx so you can see what our security ops expects. Can you please provide: a short mutual action plan, redline language you would prefer for the security exhibit, and any operational constraints that would prevent us from meeting a tight 6–8 week onboarding calendar?

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Liu
Head of IT Security
Helio Therapeutics

Attachment: vendor_pen_test_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@heliotherapy.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mchen@heliotherapy.com>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form security exhibit — pen test gating and SOC2 evidence cadence

Emma — appreciate the scope doc, that helps. High-level reply and proposed MAP below. I'll loop in legal on redlines separately.

Mutual action plan (high level):
- Week 0: finalize order form + security exhibit redlines (legal/GC review).
- Week 1–2: provide Helio with current SOC 2 Type II report, controls map, and sample artifact list.
- Week 2–4: staging provisioning, ephemeral test accounts, IP allowlist configuration, and a dry-run smoke test.
- Week 4–6: pen test (vendor or customer-led) in staging; Redwood provides an on-call security engineer and ephemeral creds.
- Week 6–8: evidence handoff and remediation notes; final sign-off for cutover.

Pen-test gating (Redwood's baseline):
- Staging environment only — no production testing without explicit addendum.
- 14 calendar days’ notice for scheduled test runs.
- Redwood will provide ephemeral credentials scoped to the test (timeboxed) and a single source IP allowlist or VPN peering; we cannot provide broad network-level access to internal infra.
- Successful completion of a smoke run (connectivity/tests < 1 hour) is required before full test kickoff.

SOC 2 evidence cadence:
- SOC 2 Type II report: available as of contract execution (we'll share current report and controls map).
- Artifacts and sample sets: Redwood can pull requested artifacts on a weekly cadence for a 4-week window following request; for a rolling 12-month view we'll provide an indexed set of redacted artifacts on secure share with access review.

Operational constraints:
- Full forensic-level access (live memory snapshots, unrestricted DB queries) is not permitted; evidence will be provided via secured artifacts and controlled sessions.
- We ask that vulnerability findings be shared via the agreed triage channel (encrypted ticket attached to the order form) and allow 10 business days for remediation before public disclosure.

I'll attach a short redline suggestions doc for your legal team to review; Karthik I'll hand off the proposed language so we can avoid open-ended inspection rights.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_suggestions.docx (docx stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@heliotherapy.com>; Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>; Mark Chen <mchen@heliotherapy.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form security exhibit — pen test gating and SOC2 evidence cadence

Emma / team — legal here. Thanks for the scope. A few concrete redline proposals and rationale so procurement can move quickly:

1) Narrow the inspection right: replace any language that allows unrestricted "on-site" or "forensic" inspections with: "Customer may request access to specific, scoped artifacts and test evidence; Redwood will provide those artifacts via secure share within the agreed evidence cadence. In exceptional cases requiring deeper access, parties will negotiate a separate scoped SOW and limited forensic session under an agreed statement of work."

2) Pen test approvals: include explicit gating language stating Redwood's security ops must approve the pen-test plan (tests, tools, and IPs) 7 business days prior to execution; this prevents tests that rely on unsafe tooling or destructive scans.

3) Data minimization & log retention: accept Helio's ask for 90 days of post-test audit log preservation for the specific test window, but limit it to logs directly generated by test activity and not all tenant logs.

4) Vulnerability disclosure timeline: propose a 10 business day remediation window before public disclosure and a coordinated disclosure clause thereafter.

5) Evidence redaction: Redwood retains the right to redact PII or tenant-sensitive identifiers from artifacts prior to sharing.

If Helio needs full access (live sessions, memory dumps), we can support via a scoped SOW and an approved on-prem/air-gapped arrangement; that's not part of the standard order form. Happy to run language by GC.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

[internal note: avoid "inspection rights" language — prefer artifact + SOW path]

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@heliotherapy.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>; Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Chen <mchen@heliotherapy.com>; security_ops@heliotherapy.com
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form security exhibit — pen test gating and SOC2 evidence cadence

Karthik — thanks, that wording is helpful and closer to what risk will accept. Two clarifications from our side:

- Retention: 90 days is fine provided we get indexable logs for the test window and a mechanism (API or secure export) to validate they were preserved. Can Redwood confirm the export format (CSV/JSON) and whether you can support a one-time export to our SFTP?
- Acceptance criteria: our vendor requires an explicit acceptance criteria doc for the test (e.g., no unauthorized escalation to production, list of allowed scanning ports, and a signed acknowledgment of test rules). Can Redwood provide a standard "pen-test runbook" we can include in the SOW?

If you can send the runbook + confirm export format, we can sign off to push the order form through procurement this week.

Emma

Attachment: vendor_pen_test_scope.xlsx (see earlier)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@heliotherapy.com>; Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Chen <mchen@heliotherapy.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form security exhibit — pen test gating and SOC2 evidence cadence

Emma — Laura from Ops. Quick operational answers and next steps:

- Pen-test runbook: attached below (brief) — we will provide the runbook as a PDF and also an editable checklist for vendors. It covers allowed ports, approved scanners, escalation contacts, and a dry-run checklist.
- Log export: we will provide test-window logs in gzipped JSONL or CSV upon request; we can deliver a one-time export to an SFTP you control.
- Scheduling: security ops will require a 14-calendar-day notice and a 48-hour smoke window; please propose three candidate windows and we will pick one.
- SLA / evidence window: Redwood will commit to producing requested artifacts within the agreed weekly cadence; if we miss the agreed evidence pickup window by more than 7 business days, we will offer a service credit (order form paragraph to follow).

I'll route the runbook and a short evidence delivery SLA paragraph to legal for inclusion in the order form. If Helio can confirm candidate weeks I will lock resources.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: PenTest_Runbook_Redwood.pdf (pdf stub)
